title: Loan Officers
description: Evaluate, authorize, or recommend approval of commercial, real estate, or credit loans. Advise borrowers on financial status and payment methods. Includes mortgage loan officers and agents, collection analysts, loan servicing officers, loan underwriters, and payday loan officers.

tasks.text: Meet with applicants to obtain information for loan applications and to answer questions about the process.
Analyze applicants' financial status, credit, and property evaluations to determine feasibility of granting loans.
Approve loans within specified limits, and refer loan applications outside those limits to management for approval.
Explain to customers the different types of loans and credit options that are available, as well as the terms of those services.
Submit applications to credit analysts for verification and recommendation.
Review loan agreements to ensure that they are complete and accurate according to policy.
Review and update credit and loan files.
Obtain and compile copies of loan applicants' credit histories, corporate financial statements, and other financial information.
Work with clients to identify their financial goals and to find ways of reaching those goals.
Handle customer complaints and take appropriate action to resolve them.
Stay abreast of new types of loans and other financial services and products to better meet customers' needs.
Market bank products to individuals and firms, promoting bank services that may meet customers' needs.
Analyze potential loan markets and develop referral networks to locate prospects for loans.
Compute payment schedules.
Supervise loan personnel.
Prepare reports to send to customers whose accounts are delinquent, and forward irreconcilable accounts for collector action.
Set credit policies, credit lines, procedures and standards in conjunction with senior managers.
Assist in selection of financial award candidates using electronic databases to certify loan eligibility.
Authorize or sign mail collection letters.
Calculate amount of debt and funds available to plan methods of payoff and to estimate time for debt liquidation.
Confer with underwriters to resolve mortgage application problems.
Contact applicants or creditors to resolve questions about applications or to assist with completion of paperwork.
Contact borrowers with delinquent accounts to obtain payment in full or to negotiate repayment plans.
Counsel clients on personal and family financial problems, such as excessive spending or borrowing of funds.
Establish payment priorities according to credit terms and interest rates to reduce clients' overall costs.
Inform individuals and groups about the financial assistance available to college or university students.
Maintain and review account records, updating and recategorizing them according to status changes.
Match individuals' needs and eligibility with available financial aid programs to provide informed recommendations.
Review accounts to determine write-offs for collection agencies.
Review billing for accuracy.

skills.name: Active Listening
skills.def: Giving full attention to what other people are saying, taking time to understand the points being made, asking questions as appropriate, and not interrupting at inappropriate times.

skills.name: Speaking
skills.def: Talking to others to convey information effectively.

skills.name: Reading Comprehension
skills.def: Understanding written sentences and paragraphs in work-related documents.

skills.name: Judgment and Decision Making
skills.def: Considering the relative costs and benefits of potential actions to choose the most appropriate one.

skills.name: Critical Thinking
skills.def: Using logic and reasoning to identify the strengths and weaknesses of alternative solutions, conclusions, or approaches to problems.

skills.name: Writing
skills.def: Communicating effectively in writing as appropriate for the needs of the audience.

skills.name: Mathematics
skills.def: Using mathematics to solve problems.

skills.name: Social Perceptiveness
skills.def: Being aware of others' reactions and understanding why they react as they do.

skills.name: Complex Problem Solving
skills.def: Identifying complex problems and reviewing related information to develop and evaluate options and implement solutions.

skills.name: Active Learning
skills.def: Understanding the implications of new information for both current and future problem-solving and decision-making.

skills.name: Time Management
skills.def: Managing one's own time and the time of others.

skills.name: Service Orientation
skills.def: Actively looking for ways to help people.

skills.name: Monitoring
skills.def: Monitoring/Assessing performance of yourself, other individuals, or organizations to make improvements or take corrective action.

skills.name: Coordination
skills.def: Adjusting actions in relation to others' actions.

skills.name: Persuasion
skills.def: Persuading others to change their minds or behavior.

skills.name: Negotiation
skills.def: Bringing others together and trying to reconcile differences.

skills.name: Instructing
skills.def: Teaching others how to do something.

skills.name: Learning Strategies
skills.def: Selecting and using training/instructional methods and procedures appropriate for the situation when learning or teaching new things.

skills.name: Systems Analysis
skills.def: Determining how a system should work and how changes in conditions, operations, and the environment will affect outcomes.

skills.name: Management of Personnel Resources
skills.def: Motivating, developing, and directing people as they work, identifying the best people for the job.

skills.name: Office suite software
skills.def: Software to provide word processing, spreadsheet, e-mail, presentations, or data management capabilities. Examples: Experian Strategy Management, Microsoft Office software.

skills.name: Electronic mail software
skills.def: Software to compose, send, or receive email. Examples: IBM Notes, Microsoft Outlook.

skills.name: Spreadsheet software
skills.def: Software to create or edit numbers or text organized into rows and columns of cells. May include formulas which recalculate values based on other cells. Examples: Microsoft Excel.

skills.name: Enterprise resource planning ERP software
skills.def: Software to integrate, monitor, or analyze data from multiple business operations within a unified system. Examples: Datatel Colleague, Oracle PeopleSoft, SAP software.

skills.name: Data base user interface and query software
skills.def: Software to query, present, or edit information stored in a database sytem. Examples: EDExpress, ELM Resources ELM, EMT Applications CounselorMax, FileMaker Pro.

skills.name: Presentation software
skills.def: Software to create presentations, speeches, or slideshows. Examples: Microsoft PowerPoint.
